Evidence and limits

The screenshots below are from this review’s development browser walkthrough. Source inspection adds paths and states that were not exercised. “Visible” means a claim is shown in a capture; “Inferred” is a conclusion from the inspected source or walkthrough; “Needs verification” identifies a risk or behavior that still needs a runtime check.

These captures cannot establish: actual desktop/native behavior, live display or NDI output, microphone input, a downloaded Bible, or populated Notes and Media workflows. Accessibility, responsive behavior and failure paths also require dedicated runtime checks. An empty browser display list is not evidence that connected desktop screens will be missing.

How to compare the three directions

Use the two accompanying interactive visuals together: one covers the main workspaces and the other covers Settings and supporting tools. Select the same direction in each visual; their selectors work independently.

1 · Compact desk

A dense, familiar workspace with settings and tools in a sidebar. Compare how much remains visible and how quickly controls can be found.

2 · Context desk

Gives the central task more room and uses a screen selector in supporting tools. Compare the focus on the selected item and the number of steps between tasks.

3 · Broadcast desk

Gives output monitoring more space and adds output context to supporting tools. Compare the visibility of Preview, Live and display state.

  1. In the main visual, use the workspace navigation to compare Bible, Songs, Notes, Media, Video Overlays and Timer. Try staging an item and using the preview and live controls in each direction.
  2. In the supporting visual, use the Settings and Tools navigation or the Screen selector to explore outputs, themes, editors and the grouped import, setup, help and recovery flows. Compare the same screen across all three directions.
  3. Look for consistent control placement, clear selection and status, and a predictable path from editing to preview. Choose a direction, then use the page index below to identify the next components to refine.

Illustrative states. Example content, transcript, staged and live indicators, output destinations, audio activity, timer, downloads, imports, key checks, update messages, confirmations and undo are design examples wherever shown. The mockups simulate selected interactions; they do not operate the actual app or its outputs. A mockup state does not establish that the current product behaves that way.

Still needs native verification. Test physical display and NDI connections, microphone and permission flows, downloaded Scripture, populated Notes and Media, file pickers, real errors, updates, keyboard access and responsive windows in the desktop app. The index distinguishes photographed states from source-only findings.

Priority findings

The first issues affect live operation or the ability to recover work. Severity is a review priority, not a measured score.

1

Make the staged item and live behavior unmistakable

Live presentationVisibleCritical

Evidence. The Songs capture shows a selected song and a preview. The preview rail does not identify the staged song by source and title outside the slide itself. Follow live is exposed as a switch; its operational effect is described in hover help.

Problem. An operator can be unsure what a preview contains or whether changing a song slide will affect the active output.

Why it matters. The same workspace is used during live service, when a mistaken change may reach the audience.

Recommendation. Label Preview with content type and title. Put a short explanation beside Follow live and the Notes loop, and show the action’s actual destination before presenting.

Evidence: Songs capture; src/components/panels/songs-queue-panel.tsx and src/components/panels/search/pre-service-loop.tsx.

2

Protect drafts and make deletion recoverable

Data protectionInferredCritical

Evidence. Source inspection shows Song Editor closes with unsaved fields without a dirty prompt; switching themes starts a different draft and clears the current dirty state; switching Settings sections unmounts the active section. Several note, set, media, song and Look removals have no undo.

Problem. A routine close, section switch or delete can discard work without a clear recovery path.

Why it matters. Operators may prepare material during a service and cannot easily reconstruct a lost draft.

Recommendation. Preserve local drafts when switching sections; ask Save / Discard / Cancel when a dirty editor would close or switch; offer undo or a specific confirmation for destructive removal.

Sources: src/components/songs/song-editor-dialog.tsx; src/components/broadcast/theme-library.tsx; src/stores/broadcast-designer-actions.ts; src/components/settings-dialog.tsx; src/components/on-display/overlay-look-dialog.tsx.

3

Give song and overlay shortcuts distinct bindings

Keyboard accessNeeds verificationCritical

Evidence. The overlay key handler listens for digits 1–9 at window capture and song slide navigation also uses digit keys. Theme cards contain interactive buttons inside a keyboard-handled card; context-search result navigation also needs a keyboard pass.

Risk. A digit intended for a song slide may instead operate an overlay, while nested or result actions may be difficult to reach by keyboard.

Why verify. Confirm event precedence, focus behavior, screen-reader names and actual destinations in the running desktop app.

Recommendation. Keep the requested overlay 1–9 shortcuts. Give song jumps a distinct, documented chord and provide a keyboard-visible shortcut reference.

Sources: src/components/on-display/overlay-pads.tsx; src/components/panels/songs-queue-panel.tsx; src/components/broadcast/theme-library.tsx; src/components/panels/search/scripture-context-results.tsx.

4

Keep output cards stable and protect active outputs

Output managementNeeds verificationCritical

Evidence. The Displays capture shows named outputs and an X removal control. Source inspection indicates a removal can stop and remove an output; the display rail orders cards by enabled state.

Risk. Controls that move after a toggle or remove a live output can surprise an operator relying on position and muscle memory.

Why verify. Verify the behavior with real display and NDI outputs, including the active-output removal path.

Recommendation. Keep a stable user-defined order, show destination and state, and require a specific confirmation or reversible step before removing an active output.

Sources: src/components/broadcast/output-card.tsx and the display rail; Displays capture.

5

Explain setup failures and offer a retry

Feedback and recoveryNeeds verificationMedium

Evidence. Source inspection shows audio device enumeration catches errors to an empty list, a failed update can become “No updates found,” and Timer background-upload failures are logged without actionable feedback. Scripture download cancellation appears only on hover.

Risk. A failed operation can look like an empty result or an ordinary up-to-date state, leaving no clear recovery action.

Why verify. Reproduce device, update, download and upload failures in the desktop app, including keyboard-only interaction.

Recommendation. Show the failure beside its control with Retry and a specific next step; expose Cancel on focus as well as hover.

Sources: src/components/settings/audio-section.tsx; src/lib/app-updater.ts; src/components/settings/updates-section.tsx; src/components/settings/bible-section.tsx; src/components/controls/presenter-timer.tsx.

6

Distinguish a suggestion from a verified match

Scripture searchNeeds verificationMedium

Evidence. Context-search rows render a percentage derived from result similarity. The reviewed source also uses rank-derived values for results; the current capture does not contain downloaded Scripture or populated results.

Risk. A precise percentage may be read as a measured confidence even when it is not calibrated for correctness.

Why verify. Check result ranking, keyboard access and the meaning of displayed percentages with real downloaded Scripture and representative queries.

Recommendation. Use a neutral “Suggested” label unless the value is validated as confidence; make the verse text, source and explicit Preview action easy to scan.

Source: src/components/panels/search/scripture-context-results.tsx; Bible capture.

7

Bring guidance and responsive behavior in line with the app

Guidance and legibilityInferredMedium

Evidence. The tutorial source references a context-search target that is not rendered and describes a click as presenting where the current interaction stages a verse. Help lists tutorial navigation rather than the wider operator shortcuts. The theme designer uses fixed minimum widths; older transcript text appears faint in the reviewed flow.

Problem. Outdated help and compressed or low-contrast controls make it harder to find and trust the next action.

Why it matters. An operator should be able to learn the current workflow and use it at the widths and contrast settings they actually choose.

Recommendation. Update tutorial targets and Preview/Live wording; add a complete shortcut guide; test transcript contrast and collapse or scroll designer panes at narrow widths.

Sources: src/components/tutorial/tutorial-steps.ts; src/components/settings/help-section.tsx; src/components/broadcast/theme-designer.tsx. Narrow, keyboard and contrast behavior still need runtime verification.

8

The graphic chooser makes unfamiliar actions understandable

What to preserveVisibleWorking well

Evidence. The Add graphic capture pairs Logo, Bar, Lower third and Scrolling text with a visual example and a short description. The new-song dialog pairs editing with a slide preview.

Why it works. The operator can compare graphic types and see the effect of song content before placing it on an output.

What to preserve. Keep the visual examples and preview while tightening spacing, adding clear state labels and using the same control treatment throughout the app.

Evidence: Add graphic and New song captures.

Next steps

  1. Compare the three separately prepared design directions: Compact desk, Context desk and Broadcast desk. Choose the direction to refine before changing the app.
  2. Protect drafts and confirm or undo destructive actions; resolve keyboard shortcut conflicts while retaining overlay 1–9.
  3. Verify Preview, Live, Follow live, outputs and order on the native desktop app with a real screen and an NDI destination.
  4. Exercise downloaded Scripture, populated Notes and Media, microphone input, import failures, keyboard navigation and narrow windows.

This report is a design and source review. It does not certify live behavior or accessibility. The related visual directions are separate from this report.
